notes: Poses now come from a library of skeletons instead of from LoRAs, and every GPU photo gets a second pass on the face. A pose LoRA was always the wrong tool for a body position: it brings its training set's bodies, framing and half a face along with the pose, and every one added competes with the likeness LoRA for the same weights, which is how three concept LoRAs on one picture melted the anatomy. The new Pose library (Settings, under Features) takes reference pictures of the poses you want, any person and any body, mature or not, and never sends them anywhere but your own machines. Extract rents a throwaway CPU pod for a few minutes, reads each picture into thirty-three joint positions and keeps only those; the picture itself is dropped once read. Give each pose a name and a line saying what it is, or let Describe write the line, and from then on the photo director picks a pose for a shot by reading those lines, while the Photo Lab lists them by name with a grip slider. When a pose is used, the picture is held to its skeleton through a ControlNet in the OpenPose convention, the concept LoRAs stand down entirely and only the identity LoRAs ride, so the pose comes from a drawing and the face from one LoRA alone with nothing fighting it. The ControlNet is one file on the volume, about 6.6GB, with Check and Install buttons next to the Kontext ones. The face pass is the other half: a likeness LoRA is judged at the face, and a face in a full-body shot is two hundred pixels of a megapixel picture, too small for the sampler to spend real detail on, which is where likeness quietly goes. So after a GPU photo comes back, a vision model finds the face, the GPU cuts a square around it, blows it up to a full canvas, repaints it lightly with the face LoRA at full strength, shrinks it back and blends it in. It runs on its own for chat photos and the Lab, costs one vision read and a short extra GPU run, can be turned off under Your own GPU, and skips itself when no face LoRA rode, when two did, or when the face is out of shot. The old picture-reference repaint and the Kontext swap remain in the Lab as fallbacks.
